paper: arXiv:2411.05576 — Zhang et al., Observation of Moire Plasmonic Skyrmion Clusters

questions.question: What are the exact nanoslit index map sigma_j and the moire primitive-cell boundary over which Q is integrated to obtain Q = -3?
questions.why_it_matters: The main text gives phi_j = 2*pi*sigma_j/N but not sigma_j; the cluster value -3 depends entirely on this map and on which sub-region defines 'one moire unit'. Without it the analytic -3 cannot be uniquely reproduced.
questions.next_step: Extract Supplemental Material S5 (critical inversion condition) and the sigma_j table; re-run box-restricted Berg-Luscher integral over the stated moire cell.

questions.question: What is the closed-form critical inversion condition (Supplemental S5) for the sign flip of the optical skyrmion number vs displacement error (dx, dy)?
questions.why_it_matters: The paper's central sensing claim is that Q flips at a precise misalignment; a reproducible inequality in (dx/lambda_spp, dy/lambda_spp) would let a follow-up theory paper predict the beacon threshold analytically.
questions.next_step: Derive the SND zero-crossing from Eq.(1) by scanning the relative phase Delta-phi and displacement; compare to the S5 formula.

questions.question: How does the quasi-crystalline (incommensurate twist) skyrmion charge behave when the integration domain is not a closed cell?
questions.why_it_matters: For quasi-periodic lattices Q per 'cell' is ill-defined; a proper treatment needs a large-window average or a defect-counting (winding) approach.
questions.next_step: Implement local lobe-charge counting (per-skyrmion Berg boxes) and report a charge histogram rather than a single per-cell integer.

questions.question: How sensitive is the reconstructed 3D polarization texture (and thus Q) to the SPP evanescent decay ratio kz/kt and to the gold permittivity dispersion?
questions.why_it_matters: The transverse-field amplitude scales as kz/kt; the paper fixes eps = -10.6 + 1.7i at 633 nm. The texture and its topological robustness may depend on this ratio.
questions.next_step: Sweep kz/kt over the physical SPP range and quantify Q stability; couple to a Drude-Lorentz gold model.

questions.question: Can the FDTD near-field maps be reduced to the analytic Eq.(1) field, i.e. does the full-wave solution actually match the six-plane-wave ansatz quantitatively?
questions.why_it_matters: The whole theory core rests on the assumption that the nanoslit-launched SPPs are well-approximated by six ideal plane waves; deviations (higher diffraction orders, finite slit width) would change Q.
questions.next_step: Overlay analytic Eq.(1) Re[E_z] against the published FDTD field (or re-run a small FDTD) and compute the correlation / residual.

next_steps: Acquire and parse the arXiv ancillary / Supplemental Material (S1-S5) for sigma_j, moire cell definition, and the inversion condition.
Restrict the Berg-Luscher integral to the paper's exact moire primitive cell to test the Q = -3 claim directly.
Add per-skyrmion local charge counting to characterize crystalline vs quasi-crystalline clusters.
Optionally run a lightweight FDTD (meep) to validate the six-plane-wave ansatz behind Eq.(1).
